answer:
In llm4j, an agent is a model given one job, written as a role: a model, a prompt that says what it is for, and optionally tools it may call. Use an agent only where the step has to write text, such as a reply or a summary. If a step only picks a label or runs a fixed rule, plain code or a classifier does it better and cheaper. Your project has one agent so far, `Helper`, using `gemini-2.5-flash` with no tools yet.
